questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
UCSD is the third highest ranked university in the US in Biological Sciences, which is my field. The possibility for me to dive further into immunological and neurological diseases was a huge motivation for me. 

Aside from the academic opportunities I was drawn by the surroundings in San Diego (e.g., climate) and the ability to socialize through my hobby (volleyball).

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: UCSD uses a bunch of different platforms that weren't that easy to navigate through. Course selection was fairly easy, but especially housing information was difficult.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Introduction from Resident Advisors in the International House.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Dorm rooms and international housing (apartments with 4 or 6 persons).

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Mandatory meal plans (3 different prices) and kitchen in apartment. The kitchen was with oven, stove, refrigerator and freezer + cupboards, but otherwise empty.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: More transparency regarding the price for living on campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
Webportal where students had time slots to register for courses. First time slot to register one course, second time slot to register a second course and afterwards everybody could register for their remaining course credits. As an international student I had to apply for pre-approval for all courses as I didn't take the required courses for the upper level courses I took. For some courses the pre-approval was pending for a long time. 

The course catalogue available didn't reflect the courses offered in each quarter.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Online video tutorial and contact information to faculties and professors.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: For the most part I got the courses I wanted, but I didn't get the courses I had planned from home, as not all courses were offered in every quarter.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply for pre-approval as early as possible and do it for all courses you even consider a little bit. Be prepared to register for different courses than you expected, as not all courses are offered in every quarter.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: As I didn't take the required courses for my upper level courses at my host institution, I had to adapt to the course material in the beginning of the courses. Some of my courses overlapped quite a bit with my previous courses, and some didn't at all. For these I had to work harder to keep up, but throughout the course I did well.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
At UCSD all courses had written exams with primarily short answers and multiple choice questions. This made it easier to study for exams than at UCPH, but in my opinion this allowed for memorization rather than understanding.

All my courses had attendance, assignments and midterms throughout the course that contributed to the final grade. This forced me to be more active throughout the course than is necessary at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Human Physiology I + II
Immunology
Neuroanatomy and Physiology
Diseases of the Nervous System
Neurostress and Mental Disorders

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Neurostress and Mental Disorders: forced me to think more about how to structure scientific experiments in neurobiology labs.
Diseases of the Nervous System: introduction to 15 of the most relevant diseases of the nervous system.
Immunology: a great go-through of the entire immunological system and how this related to the nervous system and patophysiology.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Fees to acquire a visa - around 5000 DKK. Fee to pay rent (from Danish bank account) - around 3% (= 300 DKK per month).

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Rent and groceries were especially more expensive than I expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sports clubs, all sorts of clubs and fraternities were available for students. The associations were present throughout the quarter on the main square of campus.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Commit to a sports club - this makes for great socializing with Americans (primarily) that you will stick together with throughout the quarter. I played at the Club Volleyball Team and got a lot of friendships through that - a group I had social events with and that I traveled to different other universities in California with.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: As much as possible. For me nature sights was most unique and worth of watching.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy in an academic sense. I felt that most students were younger and more immature than college students in Denmark, which showed in their habits.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Find a club so it's the same group of people you keep seeing.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Adjusting to the different course structure, where you have to make a bigger effort throughout the whole course.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Rallying behind the university's students (e.g., sports teams).

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Commit to a club so you develop relationships instead of only fleeting interactions.
Experience the culture and surroundings of the university, but know that the academics is the reason to go away.
No matter how you end up living, know that Americans and other nationalities live completely different than Danes - even though you think it "should" be a Western civilized country.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Most things will be more expensive than you imagine. Get as much information beforehand as possible, but know that you'll be surprised by a bunch of additional fees.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Academics, playing at the Club Volleyball Team, living with other nationalities and develop relationships "across borders".

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Accepting that you are away from your "safety net" and that you spend time with people and doing things that is not what you prefer.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
